Champagne Pool, New Zealand: a steaming hot spring whose shore is painted orange and grey by minerals carried up from deep within the Earth.

Layers of history in stone. These striped hills were built from layers of mud, sand and volcanic ash laid down over millions of years. Each band holds different minerals: iron gives the reds and oranges, and clays give the soft greys and creams. It’s the Earth’s own mineral record, written in colour.
